children: Canada's main stock index fell on Tuesday as rising bond yields worried investors ahead of an expected interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve, with broad-based declines offsetting gains for energy.
ended down 120.46 points, or 0.3%, at 35,582.07, after touching its lowest intraday level since July 31 at 35,405.63.

"What's affecting the TSX is the same thing that's impacting the U.S. market. It's the push higher of bond yields and the rapid realization that we're shifting to a rate hiking cycle," said Philip Petursson, chief investment strategist at IG Wealth Management.
"As yields move higher you tend to see a push lower in equity multiples," Petursson said.
Equity multiples, such as the price-to-earnings ratio, help investors assess market valuations.

Government borrowing costs hit their highest level since the 2008 financial crisis, with 10-year U.S. Treasury yields rising above 5%, highlighting the tension between fast-growing global debt loads and so far resilient economic growth.
Investors expect the Fed to hike on Wednesday for the first time in more than two years as the recent surge in oil prices raises the inflation outlook.

The consumer discretionary index (.GSPTTCD) dropped 2.6% and consumer staples (.GSPTTCS) ended 2.1% lower.

proposed North American initial public offering, Agnico Eagle CEO Ammar Al-Joundi said in an interview. Shares of Agnico Eagle dipped 0.3%, while Barrick ended 0.6% higher.
Energy was the only major sector to end higher, climbing 3.1%.

Canada will let businesses immediately write off the cost of most new capital investments for tax purposes, Prime Minister Mark Carney said, unveiling a measure aimed at strengthening the economy and drawing more foreign investment.
